top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) rest on a distinct physical idea, the magic-wavelength trap that cancels the differential light shift for many neutral atoms. It differs in kind from the 2005 comb and the 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. It has shown real results, namely millimetre-scale redshift resolution and many-body physics inside the clock, and independent laboratories have reproduced 1e-18 performance. The two-name allocation is the cleanest on the list and the citation scope is defensible. P002 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) is a real discovery, but it is supported by only one member and its many-body states are not yet understood. A prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my string theory and cosmology work is distant from atomic clocks, and I have no recorded tie to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer
